title: Modeling and Optimizing Real-Time Telescope Interaction for Multi-wavelength Observation of Gamma-ray Bursts
problem: Multi-wavelength observation of gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) requires real-time coordination between telescopes. Gamma-ray detector localizes GRB and must rapidly communicate with optical telescope to redirect observation. Minimizing time-to-discovery critical for scientific value.
motivation: GRBs are transient phenomena lasting seconds to minutes. Early optical observations capture critical emission phases. ADAPT gamma-ray telescope localizes GRBs in real-time, but optimization of multi-telescope coordination is unexplored. Progressive localization (serial refinement) could accelerate partner discovery.
method: When a gamma-ray detector spots a burst, it produces increasingly accurate location estimates over time. The framework decides when to send each estimate to an optical telescope—too early wastes its effort on an inaccurate location, too late wastes time. It finds the optimal send schedule to minimize the time from burst detection to when the optical telescope begins observing the target.
key_novelty: It optimizes the timing of progressive location updates to accelerate multi-telescope coordination for burst discovery.
contributions: Modeling framework for real-time multi-telescope coordination
42% reduction in time-to-discovery compared to single-alert baseline
Framework extensible to other multi-instrument observations
limitations: Abstract-only; specific GRB simulation models, localization accuracy evolution, and scalability to multiple partner telescopes not provided.
